title: Vercel vs AWS for Hosting Business Web Apps
verdict: Choose Vercel for websites and Next.js apps where speed of delivery and low operations effort matter. Choose AWS for complex back-end workloads, strict control over data location and networking, or large steady usage where fine-tuned infrastructure saves money.
seoTitle: Vercel vs AWS for Hosting Business Web Applications
seoDescription: Vercel or AWS for hosting a business website or web app: ease of use, scaling, pricing model, control, databases and when each makes sense.
summary: Vercel is a managed platform that deploys websites and Next.js applications from Git with almost no server management, automatic previews and a global edge network. AWS is a full cloud with hundreds of services, maximum control and Indian regions, but needs more expertise. Many teams host the front end on Vercel and databases or heavy workloads on AWS or another provider.

dataPoints.label: Operations effort
dataPoints.value: Vercel: minimal. AWS: significant unless using managed services

dataPoints.label: Previews
dataPoints.value: Vercel creates a preview URL for every branch automatically

dataPoints.label: Data location
dataPoints.value: AWS offers Mumbai and Hyderabad regions; check Vercel function and database regions

dataPoints.label: Pricing model
dataPoints.value: Vercel: plan plus usage. AWS: pay per service used

dataPoints.label: Scaling
dataPoints.value: Both scale; Vercel automatically for typical web traffic

dataPoints.label: Lock-in
dataPoints.value: Vercel is optimised for Next.js; AWS services vary in portability

body:
## A common set-up

- Website and web app front end on Vercel.
- Database on a managed PostgreSQL service in an Indian region.
- Background jobs and file processing on AWS or the database provider.

See [cloud hosting for Indian businesses](/blog/cloud-hosting-for-indian-businesses-aws-azure-google-cloud-or-vercel) and our glossary entry on [cloud hosting](/glossary/cloud-hosting).

Prices and plan features change often; check the vendors' current Indian pricing before deciding.

faqs.a: No, it hosts many frameworks, but it is especially tuned for Next.js.
For high-traffic or compute-heavy apps it can; monitor usage and move heavy workloads elsewhere if needed.
